newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S. urges India to open up government purchases.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges India to open up government purchases.

text.p: A senior U.S. trade official on Monday urged India to offer greater opportunities to foreign bidders in its government procurement process.

"One of the U.S.'s biggest interests is government procurement. Can I propose that India join the World Trade Organisation (WTO) government procurement process," Deputy U.S. Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang told a business conference.
The WTO agreement ensures free trade rules in state purchases of equipment and services.
Last month India said it would prefer that developing nations be able to retain the option of adhering to the WTO agreement and not be forced to join.

Lang said there was no plan to impose a Multilateral Agreement on Investment (MAI), currently being negotiated at the Paris-based Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), on any nation.
"There is no effort to impose the MAI on India or on any other country," he said.
He said both nations would benefit if India opened up its insurance sector, took further steps to liberalise its financial markets and formulated patent laws.

Lang said corruption in business amounted to a trade barrier. "It risks sapping the vitalities of democracy and free-market economy," he said, expressing appreciation for India's fight against corruption.
India and the United States have had several rounds of informal discussions on issues which are likely to come up at a WTO ministerial meeting in Singapore in December.
"I suggest we continue with these informal discussions," Lang said.
